rulings.challenge_claim: The koh-amar onset and the sleep-noun/year-noun disclaimer both collate correctly, but one Hebrew-to-English pairing quotes a shorter Hebrew span than the English rendering placed beside it, at 51:41.
rulings.grounds: Upheld in substance, corrected in scope: the span carries TWO such pairings, not one. At oshb:Jer.51.41 the splice re-collates byte at its cited ref and covers only the first exclamation, while the rendering set beside it, “How Sheshach is taken! How the praise of the whole earth is seized!” (web:Jer.51.41), also renders וַתִּתָּפֵ֖שׂ תְּהִלַּ֣ת כָּל הָאָ֑רֶץ, which the splice does not contain. The same fault stands one citation earlier and went unnamed: at oshb:Jer.51.39 the splice re-collates byte and covers only the perpetual-sleep clause, while the rendering beside it, “sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake up” (web:Jer.51.39), also renders וְלֹ֣א יָקִ֑יצוּ — and that unspliced clause is exactly what the sleep-noun-not-year-noun ruling leans on, so the sentence's load-bearing Hebrew stands here in English only. Sound and undisturbed on re-derivation: the onset at oshb:Jer.51.36 re-collates byte and is verse-initial, one of the chapter's four koh-amar verses (sweep: 4 verses in this chapter — 51:1, 51:33, 51:36, 51:58), and the therefore-prefixed shape it uses stands once in the chapter (sweep: 26 verses book-wide); the sleep phrase re-collates byte at both oshb:Jer.51.39 and oshb:Jer.51.57 and its digit is exact (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, both in this chapter); no ketiv/qere note falls inside 51:36-44 (chapter sites: MT 51:3, 51:9, 51:13, 51:34), no parashah mark falls inside the span, and the flanking setumah at MT 51:35 is real, correctly typed and single-witness disclosed. Further finding on the same unit: the rejected alternative grounds its rival on the Masoretic paragraphing marking no interior break across the stretch. The fact is right — the next mark after MT 51:35 is MT 51:51 — but that is mark ABSENCE carrying a rival reading in a layer that is tier-3 weak, single-witness, never a driver and never counterevidence by absence, and the sentence carries no single-witness disclosure of its own.
rulings.remedy: Two edits, one class. (1) boundary_rationale: re-splice both short pairings from source so splice extent equals gloss extent — extend the oshb:Jer.51.41 splice through וַתִּתָּפֵ֖שׂ תְּהִלַּ֣ת כָּל הָאָ֑רֶץ, and the oshb:Jer.51.39 splice through וְלֹ֣א יָקִ֑יצוּ, which also puts the clause carrying the homograph ruling on the record in Hebrew. Test the cure must pass (the test that killed the original): every Hebrew run re-collates byte at its own cited ref AND every curly-quoted WEB clause standing beside a splice renders only words that splice contains. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-ground the rival on a text signal instead of on the absence of an interior parashah mark; if the paragraphing is named at all it must be labelled tier-3 single-witness corroboration and may not be the rival's ground. Test: no mark-absence stands as evidence anywhere in the field, and the sentence limit holds. The absence-as-evidence arm recurs at 51:45-51 and should travel as one corpus-wide order, not two spot fixes.

rulings.challenge_claim: The chapter-internal recurrence is asserted as near-verbatim with a byte-tier label in the same clause, but the two instances are byte-distinct and hold only at skeleton tier, and the formula is an eight-verse book-wide object cited with no digit.
rulings.grounds: Upheld on re-derivation, both arms. The splice לָכֵן֙ הִנֵּ֣ה יָמִ֣ים בָּאִ֔ים re-collates byte at oshb:Jer.51.47 and only skeleton at oshb:Jer.51.52; cross-collated the other way, the 51:52 announcement reaches only skeleton at oshb:Jer.51.47. All four words differ: three carry a different accent and the second carries meteg at 51:52 where 51:47 carries a conjunctive accent — meteg survives accent-stripping, which is why the pair fails even at that tier and holds only at skeleton. So 'recurs almost verbatim' is a recurrence claim shipped with no tier, standing in the same clause as a byte-tier splice label that proves the quote and not the relation. The digit arm holds too: the therefore-prefixed four-word shape sweeps to 8 verses book-wide (7:32, 16:14, 19:6, 23:7, 48:12, 49:2, 51:47, 51:52) and the bare announcement to 15 verses book-wide, while the claim names one further site and no count, presenting a book-wide formula class as a chapter-internal pair. Verified sound and undisturbed: the onset splice at oshb:Jer.51.45 re-collates byte, is verse-initial and extent-matched to its gloss; the 51:46 splice re-collates byte, is extent-matched, and its year-token is correctly withheld from the date class; the closing English at web:Jer.51.51 is verbatim against the staged text; the setumah at MT 51:51 is real, correctly typed and single-witness disclosed; the only mark touching the span is that closing one, and no ketiv/qere note falls inside 51:45-51. Two new findings. First, the rejected alternative again rests on the Masoretic paragraphing running across both stretches — the same absence-as-evidence defect the abutting unit at 51:36-44 carries, undisclosed as tier-3 single-witness. Second, the stronger rival goes unnamed: this unit's own prose raises the announcement at 51:47, which is the very shape the following unit takes as its onset, so a cut there is the on-class rival — and the discriminator answering it sits in the bytes, since נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה is embedded in the 51:52 instance and absent from the 51:47 instance, and the speaking voice changes at 51:51|51:52, where בֹּ֚שְׁנוּ כִּֽי שָׁמַ֣עְנוּ closes in the first person plural, but not at 51:46|51:47, where divine address to the covenant people runs on unbroken.
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: tier the recurrence — drop 'almost verbatim', state that the two instances share a consonantal skeleton and differ in accentuation at every word, label the relation skeleton tier, and carry the object with its unit and digit (sweep: 8 verses book-wide for the therefore-prefixed shape; 15 verses book-wide for the bare announcement shape). Test the cure must pass: every recurrence claim in the row names the tier a re-collation actually returns for that pair, and every count names its swept object and unit. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the paragraphing ground with the on-class rival — a cut at the 51:47 announcement — and answer it from the bytes: the embedded divine-speech formula present at 51:52 and absent at 51:47, with the change of speaking voice at the later site only. Test: the rival is text-grounded, mark-absence appears nowhere as evidence, and the field stays within its sentence limit. (3) boundary_evidence_refs: keep oshb:Jer.51.47 and oshb:Jer.51.52, which remain argued under the corrected wording.

rulings.challenge_claim: The opening warrant is a therefore-clause belonging to none of the internal-seam classes and treated as row-internal at its other site; the sameness claim across the two sites is untiered and false in the bytes; and the two verses carrying the signature digit never enter the evidence refs.
rulings.grounds: Two arms upheld, the boundary arm refined. Untiered-sameness arm: upheld, and it is one defect with the abutting unit's, not two — the onset splice re-collates byte at oshb:Jer.51.52 and only skeleton at oshb:Jer.51.47, so 'the same formula' is untiered and false at byte tier on the same seam-pair. Evidence-refs arm: upheld on inspection — the two comparanda argued in the closing sentence stand nowhere in boundary_evidence_refs. Additionally, and this is why the shape passes machine mirroring, they are written as bare dotted numerals with neither book nor witness prefix, which resolves as neither a structured ref nor a colon cite; under the campaign convention an unprefixed coordinate reads WEB numbering, so an MT-side formula claim is carrying WEB-labelled sites (numbering is identity at both, so no arithmetic error follows). Boundary arm refined: the class observations are right — no koh-amar falls in this span (sweep: 4 verses in this chapter — 51:1, 51:33, 51:36, 51:58), and the onset is neither a word-event header, nor a date frame, nor an imperative — and neither this unit nor its neighbour states a discriminator against the 51:47 instance. But the inference that the unit is left bounded by a tier-3 mark pair does not survive the bytes: the onset verse reads לָכֵ֞ן הִנֵּֽה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה, the announcement carrying the divine-speech formula inside itself where the 51:47 instance carries none, and the speaking voice changes across the seam, בֹּ֚שְׁנוּ כִּֽי שָׁמַ֣עְנוּ closing 51:51 in the first person plural before first-person divine speech resumes at 51:52. Discourse-frame change and change of speaking participant are tier-1 signal classes, which the four header shapes tested do not exhaust; the divine closure formula (sweep: 162 verses book-wide) is not the driver here but the feature distinguishing the two instances. The defect is therefore an undisclosed discriminator, not an unwarranted seam; no respan is proposed and none is required, so nothing here needs adoption. Two new findings. First, the signature sentence is a third untiered recurrence claim in this pair of units: the digit is exact (sweep: 3 verses book-wide — 46:18, 48:15, 51:57), but the stack is byte-identical only at oshb:Jer.48.15; at oshb:Jer.46.18 the formula word stands unaccented and the closing word carries a different mark, so that member re-collates skeleton. Second, observed_substrate_signals carries no onset signal at all — both entries name closing devices — so the field does not represent the seam this unit is cut on. Also verified sound: the interior setumah at MT 51:53 and the closing setumah at MT 51:57 are real, correctly typed, single-witness disclosed and correctly subordinated; no ketiv/qere note falls inside 51:52-57.
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: state the discriminator — the onset announcement carries the embedded divine-speech formula נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה, which the 51:47 instance lacks, and the speaking voice changes at the seam — and relabel the cross-site relation as skeleton tier instead of 'the same formula'. (2) Same field, closing sentence: tier the signature claim as byte-identical at oshb:Jer.48.15 and skeleton at oshb:Jer.46.18, keeping the 3-verse digit. (3) boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Jer.46.18, oshb:Jer.48.15 and oshb:Jer.51.47 in full witness-prefixed Jer.C.V form. (4) observed_substrate_signals: add a speech_formula.* entry for the seam-opening divine announcement so the field carries the onset driver and not only the two closure devices. Test the cure must pass (the test that killed the original): the onset sentence names a tier-1 signal that discriminates 51:52 from 51:47; every recurrence or sameness claim names the tier a re-collation returns for that pair; and every verse argued outside the span appears in the refs in witness-prefixed structured form, the bare dotted shape being invisible to mirror checking.

rulings.challenge_claim: The colophon citation and date-frame disclaimer both collate correctly, but one Hebrew-to-English pairing quotes a shorter Hebrew span than the English beside it, and one sentence names the writer's own production-tiling unit rather than a textual one.
rulings.grounds: Both arms verified on the bytes. The header splice re-collates byte at oshb:Jer.51.59 and stops at the prophet's title, while the rendering set beside it, “The word which Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah” (web:Jer.51.59), also names the object אֶת שְׂרָיָ֣ה, which the splice does not contain. The register arm is right on the law: the terminus sentence names a production-tiling unit beside the textual one, and that unit has no literary-critical standing; the parent collection ends at the same verse, so the legitimate half of the statement survives without it. Worth recording because it is gate-invisible: automated register sweeping reports this unit clean, its cross-part needles covering hyphenated, possessive and part-number forms but not the bare noun as used here. Sound and undisturbed: the colophon splice re-collates byte at oshb:Jer.51.64, stands verse-final, and its English is verbatim against the staged folded text at a live continuation-paragraph fold; the setumah marks at MT 51:58 and MT 51:64 are real, correctly typed and single-witness disclosed; no ketiv/qere note falls inside 51:59-64 and the single paseq seg at MT 51:59 is count-only, so its non-disclosure is permitted; the date is a genuine header-internal date frame, and the header is rightly kept apart from the word-event shapes, its verb being the command verb and its subject the prophet. Two further findings. First, the date splice is boundary-relevant — it is the onset class this unit names — yet it is governed by a web: ref and carries no tier label of its own, though it does re-collate byte at oshb:Jer.51.59. Second, the homograph contrast is made as a bare 'twice earlier in the chapter': a cross-unit reference that is not verse-anchored, so the two sites carrying it (MT 51:39 and MT 51:57, the only two verses in the book with that phrase, sweep: 2 verses book-wide) are neither named nor mirrored in the evidence refs.
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: extend the oshb:Jer.51.59 header splice through אֶת שְׂרָיָ֣ה, re-spliced from source, so splice extent equals gloss extent. (2) Same field: drop the production-tiling clause from the terminus sentence and state the terminus against the text and the parent collection only. (3) Same field: give the date splice its own oshb:Jer.51.59 citation and tier label, and verse-anchor the homograph contrast by naming oshb:Jer.51.39 and oshb:Jer.51.57 with the object, unit and digit (sweep: 2 verses book-wide). (4) boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Jer.51.39 and oshb:Jer.51.57 once they are named. Test the cure must pass (the test that killed the original): every curly-quoted WEB clause beside a splice renders only words that splice contains; no field names a production unit; every Hebrew run carries its own witness-prefixed ref and tier label; and every verse argued outside the span stands in the refs.
